:::{#thm-ldpc-rate}
#### The rate of a regular LDPC code

Let $C$ be a $(j, k)$-regular [LDPC code](#def-ldpc-code) of length $n$.
Then the [rate](channel-capacity.qmd#def-code-rate) of $C$ is at least $1 - j / k$.

:::

::: proof

Let $H$ be a [parity-check matrix](error-correcting-codes.qmd#def-linear-code) of $C$ with $m$ rows and $n$ columns.
Count the ones of $H$ in two ways.
Each of the $n$ columns holds $j$ ones, so $H$ has $n j$ ones.
Each of the $m$ rows holds $k$ ones, so $H$ has $m k$ ones.
So $n j = m k$, and $m = n j / k$.

The codewords are the words $y$ with $H y = 0$,
so their number is $2^{n - r}$,
where $r$ is the [rank](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-subspaces.html#def-rank) of $H$.
The rank of $H$ is at most its number of rows, so $r \le m$,
and $C$ has at least $2^{n - m}$ codewords.
Its [rate](channel-capacity.qmd#def-code-rate) is $(n - r) / n$,
which is at least $(n - m) / n = 1 - j / k$.

:::
